articles.title: Satin Float
articles.summary: Woven satin sheen: long float caps and buried weft give a soft directional cloth reflection. Reads as a woven composite or brick-like horizontal grain; the rows blur into a busy ribbed textile sheen.
articles.what: Satin Float assembles long float caps, buried weft, binding knots, resin channels and raised fiber tips. Up close: A tight grid of small rectangular blocks, each roughly 30 px wide by 14 px tall, with a longer bright bar, a short dash and a tiny step notch inside, like brickwork or stacked fabric floats. Rows run horizontally with thin dark seams between. Satin shows soft bright bars; metal shows crisp bright. From a distance: Reads as a woven composite or brick-like horizontal grain; the rows blur into a busy ribbed textile sheen. No colour of its own. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Weave & Composite (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: roof, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Weave & Composite", or search for "Satin Float".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Roof, hood and hero panels: broad flats show the rows
Avoid tight curves where the grid may distort
Numbers keep their colour; the strong block grid adds noise behind thin numerals, so use bold numbers.
Clear woven-brick grain, medium contrast, bright dashes in the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, metallic, gloss.
pitfalls: Not carbon twill: a rectangular brick grid, not a diagonal weave
Not satin paint: it only changes shine, though the name says satin
Avoid: moiré at small scale, keep off tight curves.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
